What you'll learn

records.quote: We get a larger inscribed angle in measure
records.text: Notice that: We get a larger inscribed angle in measure when $\overrightarrow{BC}$ and $\overrightarrow{BD}$ are about to be congruent. $\angle ABD$ is called the angle of tangency, it is a special case of the tangent angle:

records.quote: m (∠ABD) = 1/2 m (ACD)
records.claim: The measure of angle ABD equals half the measure of arc ACD.

records.quote: The angle which is composed of the union of two
records.claim: Angle of tangency: the angle composed of the union of two rays, one a tangent to the circle and the other containing a chord of the circle passing through the point of tangency.

records.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is
records.claim: Thus: the measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of the arc between the two sides, i.e. m(∠ABC) = 1/2 m(arc AB).

records.quote: i.e. : m (∠ ABC) = 1/2 m (AB)

records.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is equal to the measure of
records.claim: Theorem 5: The measure of the angle of tangency is equal to the measure of the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc.

records.quote: Given : ∠ABC is an angle of tangency and, ∠D is an inscribed angle
records.text: Given: ∠ABC is an angle of tangency and ∠D is an inscribed angle. R.T.P: Prove that $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle D)$.

records.quote: Proof : ∵ ∠ABC is an angle of tangency
records.text: Proof: ∵ ∠ABC is an angle of tangency ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=\frac{1}{2}m(\widehat{AB})$ (1). ∵ ∠D is an inscribed angle ∴ $m(\angle D)=\frac{1}{2}m(\widehat{AB})$ (2). From (1) and (2) we get: $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle C)$. Q.E.D.
records.notes: Final line prints ∠ C instead of ∠D.

records.quote: The measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of
records.claim: Corollary: The measure of the angle of tangency is half the measure of the central angle subtended by the same arc.

records.text: In the opposite figure: ray BC is tangent to circle M, AB is a chord of tangency. ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=m(\angle D)$ (theorem). ∵ $m(\angle D)=\frac{1}{2}m(\angle AMB)$ (theorem). ∴ $m(\angle ABC)=\frac{1}{2}m(\angle AMB)$.

records.quote: Important notice :
The angle of tangency is supplementary to the drawn inscribed angle
records.claim: The angle of tangency is supplementary to the inscribed angle drawn on the chord of the angle of tangency and on one side of it.

records.quote: i.e. : ∠ ABC is supplementary to ∠ AEB .
records.claim: i.e. angle ABC is supplementary to angle AEB.

records.label: Example
records.quote: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, BD is a tangent
records.stem: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, line BD is a tangent to the circle at B, X ∈ AB, Y ∈ BC where XY ∥ BD. Prove that: AXYC is a cyclic quadrilateral.
solution: ∵ BD is tangent to the circle at B, AB is a chord of tangency.
∵ XY ∥ DB, AB intersecting both of them
∴ $m(\angle DBA) = m(\angle BXY)$ ∴ $m(\angle BXY) = m(\angle C)$
∵ ∠BXY is exterior from the quadrilateral XYCA.

misprints.notes: Same quadrilateral named XYCA in the proof; vertex order differs (AXYC is the same cyclic quadrilateral).

records.quote: The converse of theorem 5
records.claim: Converse of theorem 5: if a ray is drawn from one end of a chord of a circle so that the angle between this ray and the chord equals in measure the inscribed angle subtended by the chord in the alternate side, then this ray is a tangent to the circle.

records.quote: If we draw AD from one end of the chord AB in circle M
records.text: i.e.: If we draw ray AD from one end of the chord AB in circle M and m(∠DAB) = m(∠C) then: ray AD is a tangent to circle M.

records.label: Example
records.quote: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle
records.stem: ABC is a triangle inscribed in a circle, line AD is a tangent to the circle at A, X ∈ AB, Y ∈ AC where XY ∥ BC. Prove that: line AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.
solution: Given: AD is a tangent to the circle and XY ∥ BC
R.T.P.: Prove that AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.
Proof: ∵ AD is a tangent and AB is the chord of tangency
∵ XY ∥ BC, AC intersector ∴ m(∠AYX) = m(∠C) (2)
From (1) and (2) we get: m(∠DAB) = m(∠AYX)
∴ AD is a tangent to the circle passing through the points A, X and Y.

objectives.label: Find an angle of tangency from its arc
objectives.description: Recognise an angle of tangency (tangent ray plus chord through the point of tangency) and find its measure as half the measure of the arc between its sides.

objectives.label: Relate the angle of tangency to the inscribed angle
objectives.description: Use Theorem 5, that an angle of tangency equals the inscribed angle subtended by the same arc, to find unknown angles and prove statements such as a cyclic quadrilateral.

objectives.label: Relate the angle of tangency to the central angle
objectives.description: Use the corollary that an angle of tangency is half the central angle subtended by the same arc.

objectives.label: Use the supplementary relation
objectives.description: Use the fact that an angle of tangency is supplementary to the inscribed angle on the same chord on the other side, to find angle measures.

objectives.label: Decide when a line is tangent
objectives.description: Use the converse of Theorem 5 to show that a ray drawn from the end of a chord is tangent to the circle.
